main_text.l: tici[?] tentantur nullam inferri noxam tã ue-
rum est,quàm quòd uerisimum. Igitur nō
simpliciter,sed distinctione addita, dicitur
contagiosa elephantiasis. Etenim tria tan-
tùm habet tempora, ut cæteri exitiosi mor-
bi,principium,incrementum & uigorem:
in quò hic affectus ægrum haud dubiè è me-
dio tollit.Itaq; si qua sit in hoc agresti & fe-
rro morbo contages, illa profecto nó est in
principio,nec in incremento,sed duntaxat
in ipso uigore, quando uidelicet nó solùm
naturalia uiscera,sed & pulmones, trachea
arteria, fauces, palatum & nares admodũ
putrefacta sunt, unde teter odor, flatus tũ
expirat,quos posthac inspirant intusq; ex-
cipiunt,
qui cùm huiusmodi elephanticis
consuetudinem habent.Quæ autem tuber-
culosa est,uelut cancer occultus dicitur, ut
& ulcerosa cancer ulceratus. Et quemad-
modum hic ab atra bile adusta, ille uerò à
succo melancholico originem ducit: ita e-
lephantiasis, quæ extuberat à sanguine me-
lancholico,& ulcerosa ab atra bile adassata[?]
oritur.His addit Plinius libro,Naturalis hi-
storię,uicesimo quinto,tertium genus ele-
phantiæ, quam albam appellat, cuius me-
delam ibidem scribit esse ellebori albi radices.

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment, so it is marked cont="true". "tici" is doubtful at the top left. "adassata" is doubtful; the printed word may read "adassata" or "adaffata". "teter" is printed as "tetet" in the scan and is kept as the printed form in spelling where the context suggests "teter". The word "radices" is split across two lines ("radi" / "ces.") without a printed hyphen, so it is joined.
